Issued at 304 AM EDT Sun Jul 26 2026

Pattern Synopsis/Forecast: Basic ridge west/trough east pattern
across North America early this Sunday morning...beneath a high 
latitude Rex block in the vicinity of Baffin Island...and south of a 
strong +AO/polar vortex. Long wave trough/-PNA off the west coast of 
North America...and a strong (598dam/nearly +3 sigma) 500mb high 
south of the Aleutians (WPO is off the charts negative phase). North 
American ridging is centered over the Four Corners states...while 
eastern trough axis crossed Michigan earlier Saturday and is over the
lower Lakes and along the Ontario/Quebec border. Short wave trough 
is climbing up the backside of the western ridge into British 
Columbia/Alberta... attached to an elongated latent PV anomaly that 
comes over the top of the ridge and into the upper Great Lakes. Flow 
around the ridge is also dragging a lot of wildfire smoke from the 
Pacific Northwest and western Canada into the Midwest/Great Lakes. 
Elevated mixed layer spreading east from the Rockies and into the 
upper Midwest. Strong low level warm advection also spreading east 
across the Midwest and into the Great Lakes with 0000Z 850mb 
temperatures of 20C crossing the Mississippi River. At the surface...
Great Lakes sandwiched between a cold front across Northern 
Ontario...and a warm front snaking its way southeast from North 
Dakota/Minnesota...across the Ohio Valley and eventually off the 
coast of the Carolinas. Surface dew points well into the 70s on the 
warm side of that frontal boundary. 
   
Great Lakes will remain in between the upper high over the southwest 
and southern Plains...and an upper low over Hudson Bay with 
prevailing northwest flow.  Short wave trough will ripple southeast 
across Michigan later Monday/Monday night...reinforcing the mean 
trough downstream (and possibly splitting it into two pieces). This 
whole process just looks to slow things down... especially if a 
closed low develops in the southern branch across the mid Atlantic/
New England. As it is the northern branch becomes blocked (going 
from a high latitude Rex block to a high latitude omega block across 
the North Atlantic). May see some height rises into the upper Lakes 
beyond midweek but that evolution is definitely tied to southern 
branch troughing downstream. 

Cold front north of Lake Superior doesn't look like it will make 
much progress into Michigan today...with a broad/disorganized area 
of low pressure across the Midwest/upper Lakes by Monday morning. 
Short wave trough for later Monday will drag a surface reflection 
across Michigan Monday night...and some cooler/gusty north winds 
Tuesday in its wake.  High pressure will try to muscle into the 
region Wednesday...how successful that will be will depend on how 
stubborn the southern branch upper wave is.  End of the work week 
could see another short wave trough digging across the Great Lakes. 

Primary Forecast Concerns: 

Shower/thunderstorm chances through Monday along with the threat for 
severe storms: Have been watching some wannabe showers trying to 
pop across eastern Lake Superior/eastern Upper most of the night as a
passing short wave trough works on a low level theta-e ridge and 
associated moisture convergence. Haven't seen much south of M-68 and 
water vapor imagery suggesting subsidence is already spreading into 
northwest Lower. So will keep some PoPs across parts of eastern Upper
and northeast Lower to start the day along/ahead of the passing 
short wave trough. Will hold off on northwest Lower for now given 
water vapor presentation unless trends suggest otherwise. Morning 
clouds should scatter out with time...allowing temperatures (through 
a smoky haze aloft) to warm into the 80s. Some surface based 
instability expected to develop though there will likely be some 
inhibition as well depending on how much dew points may mix out 
(think most areas will stay at or above 60...maybe some upper 50s 
across interior northern Lower). Best chance for development this 
afternoon is probably along the Lake Superior lake breeze in Chippewa
County... and along the northeast Lower shoreline as well. 

The main show for convective potential will arrive tonight...all 
depending on how thunderstorms develop across northern Minnesota/ 
Wisconsin along the edge of the EML (saturation thickness 
considerations suggest an initiation corridor from the Boundary 
Waters and Minnesota Arrowhead southeast into northern Wisconsin/far 
western Upper.  Storms that develop should propagate southeast... 
thus the greatest threat for severe storms should be across northwest
Lower around and after midnight...with upstream convection likely 
transitioning from supercells to a squall line/wind damage threat by 
the time it reaches Lake Michigan. Will just have to see how much 
inertia this activity will have by then...and/or starts to take a 
harder dive toward southwest Lower. 

As for Monday's forecast...hard to get a good feel for that
